name: Lake Salda watershed
coordinateNote: Rounded location of Lake Salda reported by the field researcher; a regional window, not a specific sampling footprint.
condition: Fluvial/lacustrine sedimentation and Mg-carbonate investigation relevant to Jezero
literatureEvidence: Field observations and VNIR spectra of lake deposits provide a process/material analogue. This research does not reprocess the spectra or infer mineralogy from DEM values.
uses: Compare deposit types and plan observations/sampling questions for carbonate-bearing ancient lake environments.
limits: Modern water, living ecosystems and recent deposits differ from ancient Mars. This 32 km window includes a known lake and is not an approved wholly terrestrial ranking window.
withholdReason: Published lake footprint is inside this window. A current inland-water mask or approved land-only footprint was not acquired; no mixed land/water score is promoted.

name: Haughton–Mars Project station region
coordinateNote: Published HMP research-station coordinate 75°26′N, 89°52′W, rounded to five decimals; not the crater center or a precise experiment boundary.
condition: Impact-terrain reconnaissance, polar-desert field operations and instrument workflows
literatureEvidence: HMP has published field operations and instrument-testing history at an impact structure. Local terrain resemblance alone does not establish polar thermal equivalence.
uses: Evaluate observation planning and field/robotic investigation workflows in an established impact-terrain research setting.
limits: Terrestrial gravity, atmosphere, seasonal light and ground conditions differ from lunar permanent shadow. Specific deployment footprints and permits need separate review.

name: Yungay hyper-arid research region
coordinateNote: Rounded field-study region coordinate reported in Methods, 24.05°S, 69.9°W. Precision is regional, not a surveyed plot boundary.
condition: Desiccation, halite microhabitats and observation/sampling in a hyper-arid setting
literatureEvidence: The published 2018–2019 transplant study measured environmental conditions and microbial responses. Published findings are context; raw logger and sequence data are not reanalysed here.
uses: Design questions about how sampling and environmental context affect interpretation in dry environments.
limits: Dry terrestrial soil and living halite communities do not replicate Mars atmosphere, radiation or an abiotic surface. DEM slope/relief does not measure aridity.

name: Río Tinto drilling-study region
coordinateNote: Converted published deployment coordinate 37°43′30.99″N, 6°33′34.92″W; the DEM window is much larger than the drill site.
condition: Iron/sulfur-rich subsurface sampling and automated sample-to-instrument workflows
literatureEvidence: Published robotic drilling used mineralogical and biomarker analyses for ground truth. NASA explicitly distinguishes the biological analogue from a mechanical/textural analogue.
uses: Frame drilling, sample-transfer and contamination-control research questions.
limits: River, mining and biological processes require separate footprint/water/geochemical review. A high terrain index cannot establish the published biochemical analogy or rover traction.

name: Craters of the Moon volcanic-field region
coordinateNote: Smithsonian GVP volcanic-field reference point; a reproducible regional window, not the exact BASALT EVA station or the whole monument.
condition: Basaltic field-science operations and communication-delayed observation planning
literatureEvidence: BASALT-1 conducted science-driven operations in Idaho in 2016; this supports published operational use, not a new mission-specific validation of this 32 km window.
uses: Study the design of field-science observations, sampling decisions and communication workflows in basaltic terrain.
limits: Basalt origin and alteration state need their own maps/samples. Published NPS restrictions prohibit off-trail access in designated areas; no field deployment is approved by this study.

name: Kīlauea summit-region reference
coordinateNote: USGS volcano reference coordinate, independently listed by GVP volcano 332010. This is a regional DEM window, not an exact BASALT station or current hazard map.
condition: Basalt alteration and human science-operations experiments
literatureEvidence: BASALT-2/3 used regions of Hawai‘i Volcanoes National Park in 2016/2017 to study science and operational workflows. Those historical experiments do not establish present-day access or safety.
uses: Compare methods for observing basaltic environments and documenting science decisions under operational constraints.
limits: Vegetation, moisture, active volcanism and atmospheric conditions differ from Mars and Moon. The DEM acquisition epoch is not verified and may predate surface changes.
